variants.title: Guide wavelength in WR-90 at 8.6 GHz
variants.sample: Short circuit on WR-90, source at 8.6 GHz
variants.note: Near the low end of the band the guide wavelength is much longer than the free-space wavelength.

source.title: WR-90 waveguide (EIA / IEC 60153): inside 22.86 mm x 10.16 mm, TE10 cut-off 6.557 GHz

variants.title: Guide wavelength in WR-90 at 10.3 GHz
variants.sample: Short circuit on WR-90, source at 10.3 GHz
variants.note: Higher in the band the guide wavelength approaches the free-space wavelength.

source.title: WR-90 waveguide (EIA / IEC 60153): inside 22.86 mm x 10.16 mm, TE10 cut-off 6.557 GHz

variants.title: VSWR of a horn radiating into the room
variants.sample: Pyramidal horn, open to the room (never aimed at anyone)
variants.method: maximum and minimum of the standing wave
variants.note: A well-made horn is nearly matched: a small standing wave, so the maximum and minimum are read directly.

source.title: S. Y. Liao, Microwave Devices and Circuits, 3rd ed.: VSWR from the maximum and minimum of the standing wave, S = sqrt(Imax/Imin) for a square-law detector

variants.title: High VSWR by the double-minimum method
variants.sample: Slide-screw tuner set for a strong mismatch
variants.note: The minimum is so sharp that the ratio of maximum to minimum cannot be read; the width at twice the minimum power gives S.

source.title: S. Y. Liao, Microwave Devices and Circuits, 3rd ed.: double-minimum method S = sqrt(1 + 1/sin^2(pi dx / lambda_g))

variants.title: Load impedance by the shift of the minimum
variants.sample: Slide-screw tuner as the unknown load, short circuit as reference
variants.note: The shift of the first minimum from the short-circuit minimum and the VSWR fix the complex impedance of the load.

source.title: S. Y. Liao, Microwave Devices and Circuits, 3rd ed.: z = (1 - jS tan(beta d)) / (S - j tan(beta d))
